findings.reason: the node's declared scope cannot build the deliverable it is given, so the first node dispatched on §2 either reports a blocker or produces an edit_plan half-covered, and the section's own twice-per-call measure then fails for a reason the plan created.
findings.text: §2 states that `edit_plan` "is registered without the boundary scope and enters both scopes itself, twice: once around its reads before the write, and once around its reads after it", but the section's write paths name only `reckon/mcp_deadlines.py`, `reckon/mcp.py`, `reckon/metadata_index.py` and the new test. The pre-write read is `_uncovered_before_write` called inline in `_edit_plan_tool` (reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:2231-2236) and the write is `_edit_plan` (reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:1457), both inside `reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py`, which no granted path covers — a worker obeying the section literally must stop on "the change exceeds your write scope", or land an edit_plan that never enters the scopes before its write.

findings.reason: the case as written fails for every correct implementation of the boundary, so the node must either relax an assertion it was told to implement exactly or report a false defect against its own working change.
findings.text: §2's first done-when case says "One call each of these stats fewer than 300 paths and validates the covered tree once, or for `edit_plan` twice … `read_plan(view="summary")`, an `edit_plan` `set`, `roadmap(view="summary")`, `audit`, and `crew(view="live")`", but `crew(view="live")` reads live pointers, the pointer classification and the queue placements (reckon/mcp_views.py:4209-4266 → reckon/crew/query.py:396-436) and touches the covered tree zero times: with `metadata_index._reuse_covered` spied, a live view for project `reckon` made 0 calls while the same spy counted a direct call as 1. A correct implementation therefore records 0 for that tool, and an assertion of "once" can only be satisfied by a wrong one, or be quietly weakened by the worker.
